concept.whyItMatters: Before taking on the operational pain of [horizontal sharding](/concept/database-sharding), splitting a monolith database by domain (Federation) immediately multiplies write and cache capacity. Meanwhile, [denormalization](/concept/sql-query-tuning-indexes) eliminates multi-table joins on hot read paths—at the cost of keeping duplicated attributes synchronized.
whenToUse: Federation when distinct domains (Billing, Catalog, Auth) have independent schemas and don't need ACID joins across domains.
Denormalization when read-to-write ratio is high (e.g., 100:1) and multi-table JOINs dominate p99 query latency.
whenNotToUse: Denormalizing frequently updated fields (like live inventory counts or account balances) where stale copies cause correctness bugs.
keyPoints: Federation (functional partitioning): separate databases per domain; smaller working sets fit in RAM buffer pools, and each DB scales independently.
Limitation of federation: you lose cross-domain foreign keys and cross-DB ACID transactions, and a single massive table (e.g., 10B events) still needs horizontal sharding.
Denormalization: store redundant columns (e.g., `author_name` on `posts` or `order_total` on `orders`) to turn $O(\log N + \text{join})$ into a single index lookup.
Synchronize denormalized copies asynchronously via [Change Data Capture (CDC)](/concept/change-data-capture) or application-level events, not brittle multi-table triggers.

sections.content:
## Architecture & Trade-Off Matrix

| Technique | Split Axis | Solves | New Trade-Off |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Federation** | By domain/function | Monolith DB CPU/RAM saturation | No cross-domain JOINs or FKs |
| **Horizontal Sharding** | By row key (`user_id`) | Single table outgrowing 1 node | Cross-shard queries & rebalancing |
| **Denormalization** | Duplicate read columns | Expensive multi-table JOINs | Write amplification & eventual sync |
